title: Vilnius
summary: Vilnius is the capital of Lithuania and its largest city. It lies in the southeast of the country at the confluence of the Neris and Vilnia rivers. First mentioned in written sources in 1323, it is known for its well-preserved medieval Old Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
content:
Vilnius is the capital of Lithuania and the country's largest city. It is situated in southeastern Lithuania where the Neris river is joined by the smaller Vilnia river, which is generally credited with giving the city its name.

The name Vilnius was first recorded in 1323, in letters written by Grand Duke Gediminas inviting merchants, craftsmen, and religious orders to settle in the growing capital of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. Over the following centuries the city became a major cultural, religious, and academic centre of the region; Vilnius University was founded in 1579.

The historic centre of Vilnius, its Old Town, is one of the largest surviving medieval old towns in Northern Europe and was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1994. The city has a humid continental climate, with warm summers in which July is typically the warmest month, and cold, snowy winters.

title: Lithuania
summary: Lithuania is a country in the Baltic region of northern Europe and one of the three Baltic states. Its capital and largest city is Vilnius. Lithuania is a member of the European Union and NATO.
content:
Lithuania is a country in the Baltic region of northern Europe. It is one of the three Baltic states, together with Latvia and Estonia. Its capital and largest city is Vilnius, situated on the Neris river in the southeast of the country.

Lithuania has a long history as the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, which at its height was one of the largest states in Europe. The modern republic is a member of the European Union and NATO. The country has a humid continental climate, and its longest river is the Nemunas, of which the Neris is a major tributary.
